name: Learn: Custom Resources (CRDs)
objective: CKAD › Application Environment, Configuration and Security (25%). Goal: discover and use resources that extend Kubernetes — define a CustomResourceDefinition, create and inspect its custom resources, discover a CRD already installed on the cluster, and understand CRD-vs-CR lifecycle.
description: Kubernetes is extensible: a CustomResourceDefinition (CRD) teaches the API server a brand-new kind, and you then create custom resources (CRs) of that kind just like built-in objects. Learn to author a CRD, create and inspect CRs, discover CRDs already on a cluster, and reason about their lifecycle.

questions.title: Define a CustomResourceDefinition
questions.teach:
A **CustomResourceDefinition (CRD)** registers a brand-new *kind* with the API server. Once applied, Kubernetes serves it like any built-in resource — `kubectl get`, RBAC, `watch`, and labels all work on it.

**Required pieces of a `apiextensions.k8s.io/v1` CRD:**
- `metadata.name` **MUST** be `<plural>.<group>` (here `widgets.stable.example.com`) — any other name is rejected.
- `spec.group` — the API group (e.g. `stable.example.com`).
- `spec.names` — `kind`, `plural`, `singular`, optional `shortNames: [wg]` and `categories: [all]`.
- `spec.scope` — `Namespaced` or `Cluster`.
- `spec.versions[]` — each has `name`, `served` (bool), `storage` (bool). **Exactly one** version may be `storage: true`; several can be `served: true`.
- `schema.openAPIV3Schema` — in `v1` a **structural schema is mandatory** (`type: object` at the root, every property typed). Omit it and the CRD is rejected.

**Handy extras:** `additionalPrinterColumns` (adds columns to `kubectl get`), `subresources.status`/`scale`, and per-version `storage`/conversion webhooks when you have multiple versions.

**Gotchas:**
- apiVersion is `apiextensions.k8s.io/v1` for the *CRD*; the *custom resource* uses `apiVersion: <group>/<version>` and `kind: <Kind>` — don't confuse the two.
- After applying, the API server must accept it — watch for the **Established** condition (`kubectl get crd <name> -o jsonpath='{.status.conditions[?(@.type=="Established")].status}'` → `True`) before creating CRs, or you may hit a transient `no matches for kind` error.
- Deleting the CRD cascades: it garbage-collects every CR of that kind cluster-wide.
questions.prompt:
Create a CRD so the cluster understands a new namespaced kind `Widget` in group `stable.example.com` (plural `widgets`), version `v1`, served and storage, with a schema that allows `spec.size` (integer) and `spec.color` (string).

Target: `kubectl get crd widgets.stable.example.com` shows the CRD with its `Established` condition `True`.
questions.hint: Apply a `apiextensions.k8s.io/v1` CustomResourceDefinition. `metadata.name` must be `<plural>.<group>` = `widgets.stable.example.com`. Under `spec.versions[0].schema.openAPIV3Schema` give `type: object` with `properties.spec` an object having `size` (type integer) and `color` (type string).
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: widgets.stable.example.com
spec:
  group: stable.example.com
  scope: Namespaced
  names:
    kind: Widget
    plural: widgets
    singular: widget
    shortNames: [wg]
  versions:
  - name: v1
    served: true
    storage: true
    schema:
      openAPIV3Schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          spec:
            type: object
            properties:
              size:
                type: integer
              color:
                type: string
YAML
kubectl get crd widgets.stable.example.com -o jsonpath='{.status.conditions[?(@.type=="Established")].status}'   # True

verification.description: CRD widgets.stable.example.com exists and is Established

questions.title: Create a custom resource
questions.teach:
Once a CRD is **Established**, the new kind behaves exactly like a native one. You write a manifest with `apiVersion: <group>/<version>` and `kind: <Kind>`, and the API server validates `spec` against the CRD's `openAPIV3Schema` — e.g. it rejects `size` if you give it a string instead of an integer.

**The CR's `apiVersion` = `<group>/<version>`** (here `stable.example.com/v1`), *not* `apiextensions.k8s.io/v1` — that belongs to the CRD itself. The `kind` is the CRD's `names.kind` (`Widget`).

**Scope matters:** this CRD is `Namespaced`, so the CR lives in a namespace like a Pod or ConfigMap (`-n crd-learn`). A `Cluster`-scoped CRD's CRs have no namespace.

**Gotchas:**
- `kubectl apply`/`create -f` works the same as for native objects; `kubectl explain widget.spec` and `kubectl explain widget --recursive` read the schema the CRD published.
- Only fields the schema declares are accepted — by default unknown fields are pruned (structural schema), unless `x-kubernetes-preserve-unknown-fields: true` was set.
- A CR created *before* its CRD exists fails with `no matches for kind`; apply the CRD first and wait for `Established: True`.
questions.prompt:
In namespace `crd-learn`, create a custom resource of kind `Widget` named `gadget` with `spec.size: 3` and `spec.color: blue`.

Target: `kubectl -n crd-learn get widget gadget` exists with `.spec.size == 3` and `.spec.color == blue`.
questions.hint: `apiVersion: stable.example.com/v1`, `kind: Widget`, `metadata.name: gadget`, then a `spec` block with `size: 3` and `color: blue`. Apply it into `-n crd-learn`.
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl -n crd-learn apply -f -
apiVersion: stable.example.com/v1
kind: Widget
metadata:
  name: gadget
spec:
  size: 3
  color: blue
YAML
kubectl -n crd-learn get widget gadget -o jsonpath='{.spec.size}/{.spec.color}'   # 3/blue

verification.description: Widget 'gadget' exists in crd-learn with size=3 color=blue

questions.title: Discover a CRD already on the cluster
questions.teach:
On a real cluster, operators (cert-manager, Prometheus, Argo…) install their own CRDs. You discover what kinds exist without any prior knowledge of them — a classic exam move.

**Discovery toolkit:**
- `kubectl get crd` — lists all installed CRDs; add `| grep <word>` to filter.
- `kubectl api-resources` — every kind the API server serves, with `APIVERSION`, `NAMESPACED`, `SHORTNAMES`, `KIND`. Filter with `--api-group=<group>` or `--namespaced=true`.
- `kubectl api-versions` — lists served `group/version` pairs.
- `kubectl explain <kind>` and `kubectl explain <kind>.spec --recursive` — read the fields the CRD's schema allows, straight from the API server.
- `kubectl get crd <name> -o yaml` — the full CRD, including `openAPIV3Schema`, `scope`, versions, and `shortNames`.

**Gotchas:**
- The CR's `apiVersion` comes from the CRD's `group` + the version where `served: true`; if several versions are served, pick the storage/stable one.
- `kubectl get <plural>` needs the right namespace (`-n`) for Namespaced CRDs, or `-A` to span all.
- `kubectl api-resources` reflects what's *served now*; a CRD not yet `Established` won't appear.
questions.prompt:
The setup already installed a CRD for kind `Gizmo` in group `demo.example.com` (plural `gizmos`, namespaced, `spec.power` is an integer). Discover it, then create a `Gizmo` named `turbo` in `crd-learn` with `spec.power: 9`.

Target: `kubectl -n crd-learn get gizmo turbo` exists with `.spec.power == 9`.
questions.hint: Find it: `kubectl api-resources --api-group=demo.example.com` or `kubectl get crd | grep gizmo`. Inspect the schema: `kubectl get crd gizmos.demo.example.com -o yaml`. Then apply a `demo.example.com/v1` `Gizmo` with `spec.power: 9`.
questions.solution:
kubectl api-resources --api-group=demo.example.com
kubectl get crd gizmos.demo.example.com -o yaml | grep -A6 openAPIV3Schema
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl -n crd-learn apply -f -
apiVersion: demo.example.com/v1
kind: Gizmo
metadata:
  name: turbo
spec:
  power: 9
YAML
kubectl -n crd-learn get gizmo turbo -o jsonpath='{.spec.power}'   # 9

verification.description: Gizmo 'turbo' (seeded CRD) exists in crd-learn with power=9

questions.title: List custom resources by plural / short name
questions.teach:
Because a CRD registers a real kind, all the usual discovery verbs work. This is how you inventory custom objects an operator created — the same muscle memory as `kubectl get pods`.

**Ways to list the same CRs:**
- By plural: `kubectl get widgets` (singular `kubectl get widget` and short name `kubectl get wg` also work).
- Fully-qualified to avoid name clashes across groups: `kubectl get widgets.stable.example.com`.
- By `categories` if the CRD declared any (e.g. `kubectl get all` won't include custom kinds unless the CRD opted in).
- Scope filters: `-n <ns>` for one namespace, `-A` / `--all-namespaces` for every namespace.

**Output/selection variants** (all identical to native objects): `-o wide`, `-o yaml`, `-o jsonpath=...`, `-l key=value` label selectors, `--field-selector`, and `-w` to watch.

**Gotchas:**
- Short names only exist if the CRD's `spec.names.shortNames` declared them — don't assume `wg` works on an arbitrary CRD; check `kubectl api-resources`.
- For a Namespaced CRD, forgetting `-n` lists only the current/`default` namespace and can look "empty".
questions.prompt:
Create a **second** Widget named `widget2` in `crd-learn` (`spec.size: 7`, `spec.color: red`), so that listing with `kubectl -n crd-learn get widgets` shows two Widgets.

Target: namespace `crd-learn` contains at least two Widgets, including `widget2`.
questions.hint: Same shape as step 2 but `metadata.name: widget2`, `size: 7`, `color: red`. Verify with `kubectl -n crd-learn get widgets` (or the short name `kubectl -n crd-learn get wg`).
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl -n crd-learn apply -f -
apiVersion: stable.example.com/v1
kind: Widget
metadata:
  name: widget2
spec:
  size: 7
  color: red
YAML
kubectl -n crd-learn get widgets   # gadget and widget2
kubectl -n crd-learn get wg        # same, via shortName

questions.title: CR vs CRD lifecycle
questions.teach:
A **custom resource (CR)** and the **CRD** that defines it have independent lifecycles.

**Delete a single CR** — `kubectl -n crd-learn delete widget scratch` (or `delete widget --all` / `delete -f scratch.yaml` / by label `-l color=green`). Removes just that object; the CRD and every other Widget are untouched.

**Delete the CRD** — `kubectl delete crd widgets.stable.example.com` is the heavy hammer: it **garbage-collects every CR of that kind cluster-wide, across all namespaces**, then removes the kind from the API. Use it only to retire the whole extension.

**Gotchas:**
- Deleting the CRD cascades to all its CRs — you can't keep the data and drop just the definition.
- Deleting the *namespace* also deletes the Namespaced CRs inside it, but leaves the (cluster-scoped) CRD intact.
- If a CR hangs in `Terminating`, a **finalizer** is blocking it — the controller/operator must clear it (or you edit `metadata.finalizers`), not a second delete.
- On CKAD, know the blast radius: remove one CR to clean up data; remove the CRD only when retiring the kind.
questions.prompt:
A CR's lifecycle is independent of its CRD and of its sibling CRs. Create a throwaway Widget `scratch` in `crd-learn` (any size/color), then delete **only** `scratch`.

Target: `scratch` is gone, while the CRD `widgets.stable.example.com`, `gadget`, and `widget2` all remain.
questions.hint: Apply a Widget named `scratch`, then `kubectl -n crd-learn delete widget scratch`. Deleting one CR leaves the CRD and the other CRs (`gadget`, `widget2`) untouched — only deleting the CRD itself cascade-deletes every Widget.
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl -n crd-learn apply -f -
apiVersion: stable.example.com/v1
kind: Widget
metadata:
  name: scratch
spec:
  size: 1
  color: green
YAML
kubectl -n crd-learn delete widget scratch
kubectl -n crd-learn get widgets                 # gadget and widget2 remain
kubectl get crd widgets.stable.example.com       # CRD still present

verification.description: scratch deleted; CRD, gadget, and widget2 all survive
